sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the fifteen words in the verse "את הוי' האמרת" and the fifteen items of the Mishkan allude to the Name Yud-Hei, and that this represents the unification of Yud-Hei with the aspect of five hundred, paralleling two interpretations of "Havayah is One."

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what the Tzemach Tzedek brings
(in his aforementioned discourse)20
that which the Bachya writes21
that in the verse "את הוי' האמרת" there are fifteen words, corresponding to the fifteen items22
that were in the Mishkan.
And in the Bachya there,
that "the Mishkan is a paradigm of the creation of the world,
and the reason for this in the creation of the world and in the Mishkan
is to allude to what is written23
'For with the Yud-Hei, Havayah formed the worlds.'"
And this means,
that the fifteen items in the Mishkan allude to Yud-Hei
(whose numerical value is fifteen).
And from this it is also understood regarding the fifteen words in the verse "את הוי' האמרת,"
that they allude to Yud-Hei.
And he continues in the Bachya there,
that corresponding to them
(corresponding to the fifteen items in the Mishkan)
there are found fifteen times five hundred in the seven firmaments24.
And it is explained in the discourse20,
that this is also that which "Va'eschanan" has the numerical value of five hundred and fifteen25,
fifteen times five hundred.
And according to what is explained elsewhere26
that the matter of "Va'eschanan" having the numerical value of five hundred and fifteen
(where five hundred and fifteen are in one word27)
is the connection and unification of the aspect of fifteen
(Yud-Hei)
with the aspect of five hundred
(as will be explained),
it can be said,
that this that in the verse "את הוי' האמרת" there are fifteen words
(and likewise that in the Mishkan there were fifteen items)
which allude to Yud-Hei
(as above)
the intention in this is
(not to the aspect of Yud-Hei as it is in itself,
but rather)
to the aspect of Yud-Hei as it is connected and unified with the aspect of five hundred28.
And this will be understood according to the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory
(brought above)
that the matter of "את הוי' האמרת" is "You have made Me a single entity... Havayah is One,"
which has two explanations.
The first explanation,
that "Havayah is One" is as the Arizal explained on the verse29
"On that day Havayah will be One,"
that Yud-Hei with Vav-Hei will be "bound together in a single unity,"
the connection of the intellect and the emotions30.
And the second explanation is,
that the explanation of "Havayah is One" is like "I am Havayah,"
that "I" which is the Essence of Ein Sof, with the Name Havayah,
are completely one and the same31.
And this is that the fifteen words
(whose numerical value is Yud-Hei)
in the verse "את הוי' האמרת" allude to the aspect of Yud-Hei as it is connected and unified with the aspect of five hundred,
for also in the connection and unification of fifteen with five hundred
(which is in the word "Va'eschanan")
there are two explanations,
analogous to the two explanations above regarding "Havayah is One."
The first explanation,
that five hundred refers to the emotions which are below the intellect32.
For the primary emotions are the five emotions from Chessed to Hod33,
and each one of them includes ten and ten of ten,
having the numerical value of five hundred34.
And this is also that the matters in the world are in the number five hundred35,
for the root of the created beings is from the emotions.
And according to this,
the matter of "Va'eschanan" having the numerical value of five hundred and fifteen
(where five hundred and fifteen are in one word)
is the connection of the intellect
(Yud-Hei, whose numerical value is fifteen)
with the emotions
(five hundred)36,
like the first explanation of "Havayah is One."
And the second explanation,
that five hundred refers to the emotions of Arich which are above the intellect.
And the matter of five hundred and fifteen is to connect and unite Chochmah and Binah
(Yud-Hei,
fifteen)
with the Kesser which is above the chain of descent37,
analogous to the second explanation of "Havayah is One,"
that Havayah and "I"
(the Essence of Ein Sof which is above the chain of descent),
are completely one.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection of the verse to the tefillin of the Master of the World, which also have two interpretations: one referring to the drawing down of the essence of the intellect into the emotions of Zeir Anpin, and the other referring to the drawing down of Ein Sof from above Atzilus into the intellect.

translations.translation: And based on this, the connection of "את הוי' האמרת" to the tefillin of the Master of the World will also be understood
[for although in the tefillin of the Master of the World it is written "And who is like Your people Israel," which is the matter of "וה' האמירך,"
nevertheless, the two matters of "האמרת" and "האמירך" are related to each other38],
for also in the tefillin of the Master of the World there are these two matters.
For tefillin are the four intellects39,
and that which the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin,
has two explanations40.
The first,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is Zeir Anpin,
and "the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin" is the drawing down of the intellect into Zeir Anpin
[meaning,
that the essence of the intellect is drawn into Zeir Anpin.
For that which is drawn into the emotions of Zeir Anpin from the intellect as they are according to the order of the chain of descent,
is only from the aspect of the intellect that is related to the emotions,
and even this is through many and many contractions41,
to the point that in their enclothing within the emotions of Zeir Anpin they become the very substance of the emotions42,
for the intellect that is within the emotions, relative to the intellect itself, is42
the substance of emotions.
And the matter of "the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin" is that into the emotions
(Zeir Anpin)
the essence of the intellect is drawn43.
For this is that tefillin are called "Pe'er" (splendor),
that the Holy One, blessed be He, Zeir Anpin, glorifies Himself with them44,
for "Tiferes" (splendor) is a matter of being beyond comparison45].
And the second,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is the Essence of Ein Sof which is above Atzilus,
and "the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin" is the drawing down of Ein Sof into the intellect.
[And according to this explanation, the matter of the splendor of tefillin is even more understood46,
for the addition of light that is drawn into the intellect from the Essence of Ein Sof which is above Atzilus is utterly beyond comparison].

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that the verse "את הוי' האמרת" refers to the praise and glory of Hashem laying tefillin, which is brought about specifically through the service of Israel, as they make Him a single entity.

translations.translation: And this is "את הוי' האמרת,"
"האמרת" being an expression of importance and praise,
that this—that the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin
(His splendor and praise)—
is brought about through the service of Israel.
And this is "You have made Me a single entity"
(specifically "you have made Me"),
for according to the order of the chain of descent,
as it is measured by the line of measure,
the drawing down from the higher to the lower
(from the Emanator to Atzilus,
and likewise in Atzilus from the intellect to the emotions)
is contracted according to the vessel of the lower,
and in order that there be "the Holy One, blessed be He, lays tefillin" in the two explanations above,
which are analogous to the two explanations above regarding "Havayah is One"
(a single entity),
the unification of Vav-Hei with Yud-Hei and the unification of Havayah with "I,"
this is brought about through the service of Israel,
"you have made Me."
